name: Private Market Valuation
title: Private Market Valuation
answer: Private market valuation covers the pricing of equity and debt in companies that are not publicly traded, with a focus on AI businesses where traditional financials may be thin and intangible assets dominate. It includes pre-money and post-money pricing for venture rounds, secondary share sales, buyout multiples, and fairness opinions for mergers. The work supports deal sourcing, term sheet negotiation, and portfolio reporting for private equity and venture investors.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on cap table data, audited and unaudited financial statements, customer and revenue metrics, and databases of comparable private and public transactions. Valuation teams also draw on technical documentation for model architecture, training data, and compute usage where those factors affect asset value. The site's 432 company pages and 352 merger and acquisition filings provide a reference set for comparable deal activity, though private data rooms remain the primary source.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners combine income, market, and asset approaches, often using venture capital method or scenario-based discounted cash flow for early stage AI companies. For AI assets, adjustments are made for the durability of model performance, data moats, compute costs, and the risk that a foundation model becomes commoditized. Comparable company and precedent transaction multiples are recalibrated because public AI multiples can be volatile and private discounts for lack of marketability vary widely.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on data provenance, intellectual property ownership, open source license compliance, and the possibility of model outputs infringing third party rights. Valuation work must account for active litigation, regulatory exposure, and the terms attached to preferred shares, such as liquidation preferences and anti-dilution protection. The site tracks 142 active AI lawsuits and 210 compliance and regulation pages, which can signal contingent liabilities that affect fair value.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Private market valuation is moving toward more frequent, data-driven marks using automated ingestion of revenue, usage, and compute metrics rather than quarterly manual models. Standardized disclosure for AI training data and model risk is likely to make valuations more comparable across deals. As secondary markets deepen and regulators press for fair value transparency, valuation will become a continuous function tied to operational signals rather than a point-in-time event.
